default.notes: Category B nationality — apply for a consular tourist visa at a Nicaraguan embassy or consulate before travel. Nicaragua revises its category lists periodically, so confirm your status before booking.

groups.notes: CA-4 free movement (El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua) — travel on a national ID card or passport. The 90-day allowance is shared across all four countries.
Category A nationality — no visa needed. Buy the USD 10 tourist card in cash on arrival; stays of up to 90 days are granted and can be extended once in Managua.

Category C nationality — a 'consulted' visa is required, which the consulate must clear in advance with immigration headquarters in Managua. Allow several weeks and expect to name a sponsor in Nicaragua.

NI.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Nicaraguan citizens.

CU.notes: Nicaragua dropped its visa requirement for Cuban citizens in November 2021 — entry is on the same tourist-card terms as other Category A passports. The arrangement is political and could change quickly, so confirm before booking.

CN.notes: Nicaragua has waived visas for Chinese ordinary passports since re-establishing relations with Beijing, but reporting on the exact terms is inconsistent — confirm with a Nicaraguan consulate before travel.

TW.notes: Nicaragua switched recognition from Taipei to Beijing in December 2021 and closed the Taiwanese mission; Taiwanese passport holders should now expect to need a consular visa. Confirm the current position before booking.

XK.notes: Nicaragua does not recognise Kosovo, so Kosovan passports are not on the visa-exempt list — apply for a consular visa, and consider travelling on a second nationality if you hold one.
